description: Width tiers for Science Year 9–10 band — ACARA v9. Covers H-strand (Science as a Human Endeavour) and I-strand (Science Inquiry) for the 9–10 band. U-strand descriptors are in science_y9_width_tiers.json and science_y10_width_tiers.json.
subject: Science

width_notes.minimum_width: For H-strand: the knowledge-to-society pathway met in one case. For I-strand: the skill applied in one investigation context at the required level of independence and rigour.
width_notes.typical_width: Full scope across the range of contexts, investigation types, and analytical demands typical for the 9–10 band.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment adding phenomena, cultural contexts or task types. First Nations directions included where elaborations indicate them.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations treated as source data. Typical grounded in common cases; wider may infer within the descriptor's territory and year band.

AC9S9H01.minimum_width: Describe the peer review process and explain two ways it improves reliability; explain how consistent evidence from multiple studies builds scientific consensus.
AC9S9H01.typical_width: Explain the peer review process from submission to publication; examine how journals evaluate submissions; examine real cases of initial rejection then later validation (Marshall and Warren); explain scientific consensus on global warming as built from multiple evidence types; distinguish scientific consensus from public debate.
wider: Investigate the publication process for a high-volume journal like Science — examining editor evaluation criteria and rejection rates
Explore why Marshall and Warren's peptic ulcer work was first rejected then validated — examining how peer review can resist paradigm-challenging findings
Examine how Thomson, Millikan and Rutherford experiments provide consistent independent evidence for the nuclear model
Examine how First Nations fire regime data publication has informed more effective fire management policies
elaborations: investigating the process of publishing a paper in Science which receives about 12,000 submissions per year
investigating how publication of data related to First Nations fire regimes has informed fire-reduction policies
exploring why Marshall and Warren's work was first rejected then validated
examining the scientific consensus supporting global warming
researching how Thomson, Millikan and Rutherford experiments provide consistency of evidence
examining how Marie and Pierre Curie's discovery of new elements was validated

AC9S9H02.minimum_width: Describe at least two cases where technology enabled science advance; describe at least two technologies enabled by scientific knowledge.
AC9S9H02.typical_width: Examine bidirectional science-technology relationship across multiple examples; trace technology-to-knowledge and knowledge-to-technology pathways; examine Australian technology contributions; connect EM radiation properties to specific technology uses.
wider: Examine Australian technological contributions — cochlear implant, bionic eye, spray-on skin, wi-fi — tracing the scientific knowledge that enabled each
Research how monitoring technology advances contributed to the reinstatement of traditional fire management as an emissions strategy
Examine how EM radiation properties relate to uses: radar, medicine, mobile communications, remote sensing, microwave cooking
Explore how understanding of the nature of matter and energy enabled exploration from black holes to sub-atomic particles
elaborations: analysing how imaging technologies improved understanding of body system functions
considering the impact of Australian technological advances including cochlear implant, bionic eye, spray-on skin and wi-fi
researching how monitoring technologies contributed to reinstatement of traditional fire management
examining how EM radiation properties relate to its uses
exploring how scientists and engineers make machines more energy efficient
examining how advances in understanding radioactivity led to new applications

AC9S9H03.typical_width: Analyse adoption across multiple cases (solar panels, recycling, traditional fire management, assisted reproductive technologies); identify the mix of factors (evidence, economic, policy, cultural, individual benefit) driving each adoption; explain why the same scientific knowledge can be adopted in one context and not another.
wider: Investigate how First Nations fire management practices are informing and being adopted in contemporary fire management — examining adoption factors
Analyse factors driving adoption of solar panels and battery storage — examining economic, environmental, policy and social interactions
Examine how government initiatives like Landcare support adoption of land restoration practices
Research how recycling practices became widespread — examining the factors that drove transition from disposal to recycling

investigating how Dr Helen Mayo's research led to reduction in infant mortality

AC9S9H04.typical_width: Examine how funding priorities, ethical constraints, public health needs and commercial interests shape research; explain how greenhouse gas minimisation need directed science and technology; examine diverse cases including AI for IVF, green chemistry, and community-directed research.

AC9S9I03.strand: Science Inquiry — Precision and Sample Size
